Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 82, verses 1–5:

﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾, i.e., split open. ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾, i.e., they fall from their places. ﴿And when the seas are set boiling﴾, i.e., emptied out. It is also said: some of them are made to burst into others, so they become mixed together. ﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾, i.e., dug up over the dead who are in them. Al-Zamakhshari said: its origin is from "al-ba'th" (raising) and "al-bahth" (searching), and the letter "ra'" was added to it; the meaning is that they are searched and their dead are brought out. ﴿Then every soul will know what it has put forward and what it has kept back﴾. This is the response (jawab), and its meaning is: every soul will know all of its deeds. It is also said: what it put forward during its life and what it kept back, of what it left after its death, of its sunnah (a good or bad example set for others) or a bequest it made. The soul is mentioned in the singular, and what is meant by it is the generality, as we have mentioned in (the commentary on) Surat al-Takwir.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 82, verses 6–8:

﴿O mankind﴾: an address to the whole human species. ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach. Its meaning: what thing has deceived you concerning your Lord, so that you disbelieved in Him or disobeyed Him, or became heedless of Him? Included in the reproach are the disbelievers, the sinful believers, and those among the righteous who are heedless of Allah at some moments.

It is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited, "What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?" and said: "His ignorance deceived him." ʿUmar said: "His ignorance and foolishness deceived him." And he recited: ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾ (Qur'an 33:72). It has also been said: "Shaytan, who was empowered over him, deceived him." It has been said: "The concealment of Allah over him deceived him." And it has been said: "His hope for Allah's pardon of him deceived him."

There is no contradiction between these statements, because each of them is among the things that deceive a person; but some of them deceive one group, and some deceive other groups.

If it is asked: what is the connection between describing Him here as "the Most Generous" and the rebuke for being deceived? The answer: the Generous ought to be worshipped and obeyed in gratitude for His benevolence and in return for His generosity. Whoever does not do so has denied the blessing and neglected the obligatory gratitude.

﴿who created you, then proportioned you﴾: ʿAdalaka, with the letter dal either doubled or single (both readings). It means He made your limbs balanced and symmetrical, so that He did not make one hand longer than the other, nor one eye larger than the other, nor one of them blue-eyed while the other is dark, nor some limbs white and others black, and similar kinds of balance.

﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾: the prepositional phrase (majrūr) is connected to rakkabaka ("assembled you"), and mā is extra (zāʾidah). The meaning: He assembled you in whatever form He willed, of beauty or ugliness, tallness or shortness, maleness or femaleness, and other differences of form. It is also possible that the prepositional phrase is connected to an omitted verb, its implied sense being: "He assembled you existing in whatever form." It has also been said that it is connected to ʿadalaka, on the basis that the meaning is "He turned you to whatever form He willed." This is far-fetched, and it is only possible with the reading ʿadalaka with a single dal.

"Nay! Rather, you deny the Recompense." This is a rebuke of the arrogance mentioned earlier and of the denial mentioned afterwards. ﴿Nay! Rather, you deny the Recompense﴾: this is addressed to the disbelievers. Here "al-din" (the Recompense) may mean the sharia (religious law), or the reckoning, or the requital.

﴿Indeed, over you are watchers﴾: meaning the angels who record the deeds of the children of Adam. ﴿Noble, recording, they know what you do﴾: they know the deeds because they witness them. As for what is not seen or heard, such as thoughts, intentions and remembrance in the heart, it is said that Allah alone has knowledge of these; and it is said that the angel finds a scent of them by which he perceives them.

﴿Indeed the righteous are in bliss﴾: in this verse and what follows there are rhetorical devices of correspondence (tibaq) and rhyming prose (tarsi').

﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾: there are two opinions regarding it. The first: its meaning is that they will not be removed from it once they have entered it. The second: they will not be absent from it in the barzakh before entering it, because they are presented to it morning and evening.

﴿And what could make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾: an exaltation of it and an expression of its awesomeness. He repeated it for emphasis, and the meaning is that because of its severity no one knows the extent of its terror and greatness.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 82, verse 19:

﴿On that Day no soul will have power to benefit another soul in anything﴾. That is, no one will be able to bring benefit to anyone. It is read as "yawmu" in the nominative, as a substitution (badal) for "yawm al-din" (the Day of Judgment), or by supposing an implied subject (mubtada'). It may also be read in the accusative as an adverbial of time (zarf), with an implied verb whose estimated form is "yujaziyna yawma al-din" (they will be recompensed on the Day of Judgment), or in the accusative as a direct object (maf'ul bihi), with an implied verb whose estimated form is "udhkur" (remember). It is also permissible for it to be given a fatha because it is attached to a non-declinable noun (mabni), while being in a position of nominative case (raf').
